rules: Perspective is the lens's, transferred, not constructed; 24 mm used close extends depth: on a 48 cm sheet the hand at 0.6 m is ~0.83 life size, a blade at 10 cm 6.3x, the Moon 22 px (Wikipedia Hyperrealism, Perspective distortion; derived)

Depth of field added: blur b = f^2|s-d|/(N d (s-f)); at 24 mm focused 0.6 m, f/16 gives a sharp zone 0.4-1.2 m, Moon blur 6 px, grass at 10 cm 31 px, at 5 cm 69 px (thin-lens optics; derived table in doc)
FLAG: shallow focus at f/2.8-f/5.6 smears the Moon (blur >= its size); use f/11-f/22, f/16 recommended (derived)
Blur grows continuously with each object's distance; no uniform blur field, no cut-out subject (Eclectic Light on Renoir; Wikipedia DOF)
Blur is an edge width, not a value change: blurred things keep their value; thin things narrower than their blur fade to translucent grey (judgement; derived)
Points of light become aperture-shaped discs, polygonal when stopped down; matte surfaces make soft bands (Wikipedia Bokeh; judgement)
Decide the blur before detail; smudge, then detail only in focus (Dessindigo; Wildlife Art Store)
No aerial perspective at these depths; corners of a wide frame stretch round things 1.2-1.35x and darken slightly (derived; vignetting judgement)
keep: overlap order near grass > hand > sky and Moon
relative size by distance from one lens
one eye level and one lens for the sheet
avoid: mixing lenses (telephoto Moon in a wide frame)
near blur drawn lighter or hazier
cut-out sharp subject on uniform blur
sharp edges outside the focal zone
sources: Eclectic Light, depth of field in painting: https://eclecticlight.co/2023/10/13/painting-on-the-edge-depth-of-field/
